newsitem.title: USA: Don't cut CRP because of deferrals - USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Don't cut CRP because of deferrals - USDA's Glickman.

text.p: The Clinton administration plan to defer enrollment of two million acres into the Conservation Reserve should not be used as an excuse to cut funding for the program, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Monday.
"I hope that doesn't take place," Glickman told reporters. "My belief is...the CRP (Conservation Reserve Program) is the most important land management effort the government is doing now."
The one-year CRP deferral would offset $65 million that would halt development of a gold mine near Yellowstone Park.
The proposal has been unpopular on Capitol Hill but must be approved by Congress.
Glickman said the delay in enrolling two million acres would not harm CRP at all.

The CRP has been cited occasionally as a potential target for spending cuts. At least one opponent of a USDA proposal for $390 million in meat-inspection user fees has suggested taking the money from CRP, which costs $1.9 billion a year.

Glickman declined to say how much land the Agriculture Department would accept for Conservation Reserve enrollment this year. Farmers have until the end of this month to submit bids to put land in the long-term cropland retirement plan.
USDA budget documents indicate up to 19 million acres might be accepted.
Paul Johnson, head of the Natural Resources Conservation Service, said the level of interest in farm country "is exceeding our expectations."
"We're probably on track to get there (19 million enrolled acres) with the interest that's been expressed so far," Johnson said.
